title: The Impact of ChatGPT as a Brainstorming Tool on Gifted Students’ Persuasive Writing
extended_summary:
This paper examines whether ChatGPT 3.5 can function as a prewriting brainstorming tool to improve persuasive writing quality. The authors focus on a narrowly defined use of generative AI: not as a teacher-facing planning or feedback system, but as a student-facing ideation aid used before drafting. The study is motivated by concerns that gifted writers may experience perfectionism, difficulty generating ideas, and pressure from expectations, which can hinder writing performance.

The intervention was tested with five gifted senior students majoring in Arabic in the College of Education at Kuwait University. The researchers used an integrated single-subject design with multiple probes across multiple baselines, with students writing persuasive essays across baseline, intervention, and maintenance phases. During intervention, students received explicit instruction and practice on using ChatGPT 3.5 for brainstorming, then used it for 20 minutes before writing each essay. Quantitative outcomes were rated with an adapted persuasive essay rubric, and qualitative social-validity data were collected through a focus group interview.

Results showed that all participants improved from baseline to intervention, with gains especially strong in rhetorical dimensions such as argumentation, supporting evidence, opposing viewpoints, and voice/tone. Most students maintained gains three weeks later, though one twice-exceptional student showed no maintenance increase. In focus group data, students reported that ChatGPT was efficient, generated abundant ideas, and was helpful for difficult or socially sensitive topics, but they also noted limitations such as repetition, outdated information, and the need to verify AI-generated ideas. The authors conclude that ChatGPT 3.5 can complement traditional brainstorming, while emphasizing careful, critical use rather than dependency.

identified_tools.name: ChatGPT
identified_tools.description: OpenAI's conversational generative AI chatbot for interactive dialogue and text generation.
identified_tools.use_case: Used as a prewriting brainstorming tool (ChatGPT 3.5) to help gifted Arabic-speaking senior students generate ideas before writing persuasive essays.

findings.finding_summary: In a single-subject multiple-baseline study with five gifted students, persuasive writing quality increased for all participants after ChatGPT 3.5 was introduced as a brainstorming tool. Mean essay scores rose from baseline to intervention for each student, and the authors reported PND = 100% for all five participants, indicating a strong functional relation between the intervention and writing performance.
findings.measure: Overall quality of persuasive essays (Persuasive Essay Rubric; 0-48)

findings.finding_summary: Detailed rubric scores showed large gains in persuasive-writing-specific components after ChatGPT 3.5 brainstorming, especially argument, supporting evidence, opposing viewpoints, and voice/tone. General writing components such as organization, word choice, sentence fluency, and conventions changed little by comparison.

Effects generally persisted at maintenance 3 weeks later. Four of five students showed continued improvement or retention of gains; one twice-exceptional student showed no additional gain from intervention to maintenance (maintenance mean remained 36).

quality_tier_rationale: This is a small single-subject intervention study with repeated measures and staggered baselines, which provides causal evidence but not the breadth or randomization of a blue-tier design. The sample is very small (n=5), limiting generalizability.
impact_tier_rationale: Reported gains were large in the primary outcome, with PND reported as 100% and clear score increases for all participants. The study attributes substantial improvement in persuasive writing quality to the ChatGPT brainstorming intervention.
